_: Name, description and badge live in src/resources/connectors.json so the console and the browser process cannot disagree about them.

notes: A personal token is the simpler path for one workspace and is what Flux offers first; OAuth is for connecting more than one account or for a build shared with other people.
Scopes are comma-separated in the authorize URL, not space-separated.
admin is deliberately not requested. Nothing Flux does needs admin endpoints, and a token that carries it can reconfigure the workspace.
Linear is GraphQL-only: one endpoint, and the operation is the query.

personal_token.label: Personal API key
personal_token.where: linear.app > Settings > Security & access > Personal API keys.
notes: Sent as the Authorization header value directly, without a Bearer prefix - unlike the OAuth token.

query_issues.notes: GraphQL query. Everything read goes through this one endpoint.

create_issue.notes: issueCreate mutation. Draft rather than send: an issue is visible internally but is not an outbound message.

rate_limits.note: Complexity-based rather than request-based: a deeply nested GraphQL query costs more than several shallow ones. Request only the fields you need.
